column1: # Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam — Hadith 41: “Until his desire follows what I have brought”

column2: From ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“None of you believes until his desire follows what I have brought.” The Shaykh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: A good and authentic (ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ) hadith; we have narrated it in the book al-Ḥujjah with an authentic chain.

By the author of the book al-Ḥujjah he means Shaykh Abū al-Fatḥ Naṣr ibn Ibrāhīm al-Maqdisī al-Shāfiʿī, the jurist and ascetic who settled in Damascus. This book of his is al-Ḥujjah ʿalā Tārik al-Maḥajjah (“The Proof against One Who Abandons the Clear Path”), which sets out the foundations of the religion according to the principles of the people of hadith and the Sunnah.

The ḥāfiẓ Abū Nuʿaym recorded this hadith in his book al-Arbaʿīn, having stipulated at its beginning that its hadiths would be among the authentic reports and excellent narrations whose transmitters' integrity the transmitters agree upon,
and which the imams have recorded in their Musnads. He then recorded it from al-Ṭabarānī: Abū Zayd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥātim al-Murādī told us,
Nuʿaym ibn Ḥammād told us, ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Thaqafī told us, from Hishām ibn Ḥassān, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, from ʿUqbah ibn Aws, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “None of you believes until his desire follows what I have brought, not swerving from it.”

The ḥāfiẓ Abū Bakr ibn ʿĀṣim al-Iṣbahānī narrated it from Ibn Wārah, from Nuʿaym ibn Ḥammād: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Thaqafī told us: One of our shaykhs told us — Hishām or someone else — from Ibn Sīrīn; and he mentioned it.
His version does not have “not swerving from it”. The ḥāfiẓ Abū Mūsā al-Madīnī said: The narrations from Nuʿaym disagree over this hadith; it has also been given as:
One of our shaykhs told us: Hishām or someone else told us.

I say: Declaring this hadith authentic is very far-fetched, for several reasons. One is that it is a hadith that Nuʿaym ibn Ḥammād al-Marwazī alone narrates. Although a number of the imams declared this Nuʿaym reliable
and al-Bukhārī recorded from him, the imams of hadith thought well of him because of his firmness in the Sunnah and his vigour in refuting the people of heresies;
yet they attributed to him a tendency to err and to be confused in some hadiths, and when they came across his munkar (objectionable) narrations more and more often, they judged him weak.

Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad the ḥāfiẓ narrated from Ibn Maʿīn that he was asked about him and said: He is nothing, but he is a man of the Sunnah. Ṣāliḥ said: He used to narrate from memory, and he has many munkar narrations in which no one corroborates him.
Abū Dāwūd said: Nuʿaym has about twenty hadiths from the Prophet ﷺ that have no basis. Al-Nasāʾī said: Weak.
Once he said: Not reliable.
And once he said: His solitary narrations from well-known imams have become so many, in so many hadiths, that he has fallen to the level of one who is not relied on as proof.

Abū Zurʿah al-Dimashqī said: He connects hadiths that others narrate as stopping short — meaning that he turns mawqūf reports (those stopping short of the Prophet ﷺ) into marfūʿ ones (attributed to the Prophet ﷺ). Abū ʿArūbah al-Ḥarrānī said: His case is obscure. Abū Saʿīd ibn Yūnus said: He narrated munkar hadiths from reliable narrators,

and others accused him of fabricating hadith. And where were the students of ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Thaqafī, the students of Hishām ibn Ḥassān and the students of Ibn Sīrīn, that Nuʿaym alone should narrate this hadith?

Another reason is that the narrations from Nuʿaym differ over its chain. It is narrated from him: from al-Thaqafī, from Hishām. It is also narrated from him: from al-Thaqafī: One of our shaykhs told us — Hishām or someone else; and on this narration the identity of al-Thaqafī's shaykh is not known.

It is also narrated from him: from al-Thaqafī: One of our shaykhs told us: Hishām or someone else told us. On this narration al-Thaqafī narrated it from an unknown shaykh, and his shaykh narrated it from someone unspecified, so the unknowns in its chain multiply.

Another reason is that its chain contains ʿUqbah ibn Aws al-Sadūsī al-Baṣrī, who is also called Yaʿqūb ibn Aws. Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah recorded from him a hadith from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr — or, it is said,

ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar — and its chain is confused. Al-ʿIjlī, Ibn Saʿd and Ibn Ḥibbān declared him reliable, and Ibn Khuzaymah said: Ibn Sīrīn, for all his eminence, narrated from him. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: He is unknown.

Al-Ghallābī said in his Tārīkh: They claim that he did not hear from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, and only says, “ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr said.” On this basis his narrations from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr would be broken. And Allah knows best.

As for the meaning of the hadith, it is that a person is not a believer with the complete faith that is obligatory until his love follows what the Messenger ﷺ brought — commands, prohibitions and the rest — so that he loves what he commanded and dislikes what he forbade.
The Qurʾān has come with the like of this in more than one place.

The Exalted says: “But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what is disputed between them, then find in themselves no discomfort at what you have decided, and submit completely” [al-Nisāʾ 4:65].
And the Exalted says: “It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, to have any choice in their matter” [al-Aḥzāb 33:36].

He, Glorified is He, has condemned those who dislike what Allah loves or love what Allah dislikes, saying: “That is because they disliked what Allah sent down, so He made their deeds worthless” [Muḥammad 47:9]; and the Exalted says: “That is because they followed what angers Allah and disliked His good pleasure, so He made their deeds worthless” [Muḥammad 47:28].
Every believer must therefore love what Allah loves, with a love that leads him to do whatever of it is obligatory on him; if the love grows until he does whatever of it is recommended,

that is an extra merit. And he must dislike what Allah the Exalted dislikes, with an aversion that leads him to refrain from whatever of it is unlawful for him; if the aversion grows until it leads him to refrain from what is disliked only as mildly disapproved, that is an extra merit.
It is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs that he ﷺ said:

“None of you believes until I am dearer to him than himself, his child, his family and all people.” So the believer is not a believer until he puts love of the Messenger before love of all creation; and love of the Messenger follows from love of the One who sent him.
True love requires following and agreeing [with the beloved] in loving what he loves and hating what he hates. He, the Mighty and Majestic, says:

“Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your wives, your kin, the wealth you have acquired, the trade whose decline you fear and the dwellings you are pleased with are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His path, then wait until Allah brings about His command” [al-Tawbah 9:24].
And the Exalted says: “Say: If you love Allah, follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins” [Āl ʿImrān 3:31]. Al-Ḥasan said: The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ said:
Messenger of Allah, we love our Lord intensely. And Allah wished to set a sign for love of Him, so Allah revealed this verse.
In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, the Prophet ﷺ said: “There are three things: whoever has them finds the sweetness of faith — that Allah and His Messenger are dearer to him than anything else,
that he loves a person, loving him only for Allah's sake, and that he hates to return to disbelief after Allah has saved him from it, as he would hate to be thrown into the Fire.”
When someone loves Allah and His Messenger with a true love from the heart, that obliges him to love in his heart what Allah and His Messenger love,

to dislike what Allah and His Messenger dislike, to be pleased with what pleases Allah and His Messenger and angered by what angers Allah and His Messenger, and to act with his limbs according to this love and hatred.
If he does anything with his limbs that goes against that — if he commits something that Allah and His Messenger dislike, or leaves something that Allah and His Messenger love,
while it is obligatory and he is able to do it — that shows that his obligatory love is deficient. He must repent of it and return to completing the love that is obligatory.

Abū Yaʿqūb al-Nahrajūrī said: Everyone who claims to love Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, but does not conform to Allah in His command, his claim is false; and every lover who does not fear Allah is deluded.
Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh said: Whoever claims to love Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and does not keep His limits is not truthful.
Ruwaym was asked about love, and he said: Conformity in every state. And he recited:
If you told me, “Die,” I would die, hearing and obeying, / and say to death's summoner: Welcome!
One of the early poets said:
You disobey God while claiming to love Him: / by my life, by any measure that is monstrous.
Were your love true, you would obey Him; / the lover is obedient to the one he loves.

All acts of disobedience, then, arise from putting the desires of the self before love of Allah and His Messenger. Allah has described the idolaters as following desire in a number of places in His Book.

The Exalted says: “If they do not respond to you, know that they are only following their desires; and who is further astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah?” [al-Qaṣaṣ 28:50].
Likewise innovations arise only from putting desire before the Sharīʿah, and that is why their adherents are called the people of desires (ahl al-ahwāʾ).
Likewise sins occur only from putting desire before love of Allah and love of what He loves.
The same holds for love of people: it must follow what the Messenger ﷺ brought.

The believer must love Allah and love those whom Allah loves — the angels, the messengers, the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous in general. That is why one of the signs of finding the sweetness of faith is loving a person, loving him only for Allah's sake. And it is unlawful to befriend the enemies of Allah
and those whom Allah dislikes in general; this has been discussed elsewhere. In this way the religion becomes entirely for Allah.

“Whoever loves for Allah, hates for Allah, gives for Allah and withholds for Allah has completed faith.” But whoever loves, hates, gives and withholds for the desire of his own self has a deficiency in his obligatory faith,

and he must repent of it and return to following what the Messenger ﷺ brought: putting love of Allah and His Messenger, and whatever pleases Allah and His Messenger, before the desires of the self and all its wants.
Wuhayb ibn al-Ward said: It has reached us — and Allah knows best — that Mūsā (peace be upon him) said: My Lord, counsel me.

He said: I counsel you regarding Me. He said it three times, until the last time He said: I counsel you regarding Me that no matter should present itself to you but you prefer love of Me in it to everything else. Whoever does not do that, I will not purify him and I will not have mercy on him.

The well-known use of hawā, when it is used without qualification, is for inclination towards what is contrary to the truth, as in His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: “Do not follow desire, lest it lead you astray from the path of Allah” [Ṣād 38:26]; and He said: “But as for one who feared standing before his Lord and forbade the soul its desire, Paradise will be the refuge” [al-Nāziʿāt 79:40–41].

Hawā is sometimes used to mean love and inclination in general, including inclination towards the truth and towards other things; and it is sometimes used to mean love of the truth in particular and submission to it. Ṣafwān ibn ʿAssāl was asked:
Did you hear the Prophet ﷺ mention hawā? He said: A Bedouin asked him about a man who loves a people but has not caught up with them, and he said: “A person will be with those he loves.”

When His words, Mighty and Majestic is He, were revealed, “You may put off whichever of them you will and take to yourself whichever you will” [al-Aḥzāb 33:51], ʿĀʾishah said to the Prophet ﷺ: I see your Lord hastening to fulfil your wish (hawāk).

ʿUmar said, about the consultation over the captives of Badr: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ inclined to what Abū Bakr said and did not incline to what I said. This hadith is one of those in which hawā is used in the sense of praiseworthy love.

The like of this occurs often in the Israelite reports, and the words and allusions of the shaykhs of the [Sufi] folk, in verse and prose, frequently use it in this way. Among what fits the meaning of the hadith is the saying of one of them:
The love of you that is in my heart / has made me one who hears and obeys.
You took my heart, and my eye's closing; / you robbed me of sleep and slumber.
[I said:] Leave my heart and take my sleep. / He said: No — rather the two together.
